task: Review all five sections and all three sourced Insights.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Costco operates membership warehouses and e‑commerce sites that focus on low prices for a limited assortment of national and private‑label products, driving high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover. This model enables the company to profit at lower gross margins than many peers and to capture early‑payment discounts by often selling inventory before payment is due. [[source:K:L129]]

sections.title: Market Positioning and Growth Outlook
sections.text: Revenue expanded at a double‑digit percent rate [[COST.ratio.revenue_growth]], while operating margin remained in the low single‑digit percent range [[COST.ratio.operating_margin]], reflecting the low‑margin, high‑volume strategy. Return on equity was in the high‑twenties percent range [[COST.ratio.return_on_average_equity]], indicating strong profitability relative to shareholders’ capital. Leverage is modest, with debt‑to‑equity under two‑tenths of a times equity [[COST.ratio.debt_to_equity]], and free cash flow was robust at roughly nine billion dollars [[COST.ratio.free_cash_flow]]. Employee retention is high, with a one‑year tenure rate near ninety‑four percent [[source:K:L191]], and hourly wages were raised to an average of about thirty‑three dollars per hour [[source:K:L195]]. Competitive pressures arise from the need to balance pricing authority with cost increases, which can compress margins if the company absorbs costs or passes them to members [[source:Q:L651]].

sections.title: Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations
sections.text: The company plans to expand its warehouse footprint in existing and new markets and to integrate acquisitions, but execution risk could affect results [[source:K:L233]]. Enhancing cybersecurity defenses is critical given rising threat sophistication and potential operational disruption [[source:K:L253]]. Maintaining privacy and data‑security compliance will be essential to avoid reputational and regulatory fallout [[source:K:L252]]. Ongoing litigation, including pending opioid‑related claims, should be monitored to manage contingent liabilities [[source:Q:L508]]. Continued investment in employee development and compensation will support high retention and productivity. Management should balance pricing strategies to preserve the perception of pricing authority while protecting margin performance.

sections.title: Valuation Insights
sections.text: Costco delivers a modest operating margin of [[COST.ratio.operating_margin]] while generating a robust return on average equity of [[COST.ratio.return_on_average_equity]]. Its capital structure is conservative, with a debt‑to‑equity ratio of [[COST.ratio.debt_to_equity]], far lower than peers such as Walmart and Target. Free cash flow stands strong at [[COST.ratio.free_cash_flow]], supporting ongoing investment and shareholder returns. Revenue grew at a double‑digit pace of [[COST.ratio.revenue_growth]], yet the annual price‑earnings multiple of [[COST.ratio.price_earnings]] is elevated, reflecting market expectations for continued growth. Compared with Walmart’s operating margin of [[WMT.ratio.operating_margin]] and Target’s margin of [[TGT.ratio.operating_margin]], Costco’s margin is slightly lower, but its superior ROE and lower leverage suggest efficient use of capital. The combination of solid cash generation, low leverage, and high ROE positions Costco favorably, though the premium valuation warrants monitoring of future earnings momentum.

insight.text: The low debt‑to‑equity ratio highlights Costco’s capacity to absorb higher financing costs and fund strategic initiatives.

sections.title: Investment Recommendation
sections.text: Costco’s membership‑warehouse model delivers durable high‑volume sales and strong cash generation. The company posts a return on average equity of [[COST.ratio.return_on_average_equity]], indicating superior profitability on shareholders’ capital. Its debt‑to‑equity of [[COST.ratio.debt_to_equity]] reflects a conservative capital structure, providing flexibility to fund expansion and absorb cost pressures. Revenue growth remains double‑digit [[COST.ratio.revenue_growth]], while operating margin stays in the low single‑digit range [[COST.ratio.operating_margin]], consistent with its low‑margin strategy. Valuation is elevated, as shown by a price‑earnings multiple of [[COST.ratio.price_earnings]], which may constrain near‑term upside. Nonetheless, the combination of durable business fundamentals, high ROE and low leverage supports a positive outlook, outweighing the valuation premium. Risks include pricing pressure, execution of new warehouses, cybersecurity and litigation, as noted in the research sections [source:Q:L651], [source:K:L233], [source:K:L253], and [source:Q:L508]. Accordingly, the recommendation is Buy.

COSTCO WHOLESALE CORPORATION REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL YEAR 2026 OPERATING RESULTS
ISSAQUAH, Wash., September 24, 2026 - Costco Wholesale Corporation (“Costco” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: COST) today announced its operating results for the 16-week fourth quarter and the 52-week fiscal year ended August 30, 2026.
Net sales for the quarter increased 11.2 percent, to $93.9 billion, from $84.4 billion last year. Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.
Comparable sales for the fourth quarter and fiscal year were as follows:
